drills.prompt: Two flat glass plates {Lc:num1} cm long touch at one end and are held apart by a fiber {Dh} μm thick at the other. In {lam} nm light, how far apart are the dark fringes, in mm to 3 significant figures?
drills.solution:
Neighboring dark fringes are where the gap thickness differs by $\lambda/2$, and the gap grows by $D/L$ per unit length, so $\Delta x = \dfrac{\lambda L}{2D}$.

$\Delta x = \dfrac{({lam}\times10^{-9})({Lc:num1}\times10^{-2})}{2({Dh}\times10^{-6})}\text{ m} =$ **{dx:sig3} mm**.

drills.title: Resolving two close spectral lines
drills.prompt: Two spectral lines are at {lam:dp0}.00 nm and {lam2:num2} nm. Find the resolving power needed to separate them, and the number of grating lines that must be illuminated in order {mo}, each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$R = \dfrac{\lambda}{\Delta\lambda}$, using the average wavelength: $R = \dfrac{{lam:dp0} + {dl:num2}/2}{{dl:num2}} =$ **{R:sig3}**.

$R = Nm$, so $N = R/m = {R:sig4}/{mo} =$ **{Nmin:sig3}** lines.

drills.title: Bragg angles
drills.prompt: X-rays of wavelength {lam} nm reflect from crystal planes {dsp:num3} nm apart. Find the order-{mo} Bragg angle (measured from the planes) and the total angle through which the beam is deflected, in degrees to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Bragg's law: $2d\sin\theta = m\lambda$, so $\sin\theta = \dfrac{{mo}({lam})}{2({dsp:num3})}$ and $\theta =$ **{th:sig3}°** from the planes.

The beam turns through $2\theta =$ **{dev:sig3}°**.

drills.title: Two separated thin lenses
drills.prompt: Light meets a thin lens with $f_1 = {f1}$ cm, then travels {sep} cm to a second thin lens with $f_2 = {f2}$ cm. Find the effective focal length of the pair and the back focal distance (from the second lens), in cm to 3 significant figures (include the sign).
drills.solution:
$M = L_2T L_1$. Multiplying, $A = 1 - \dfrac{d}{f_1} = {Aa:sig4}$ and $C = -\dfrac{1}{f_1} - \dfrac{A}{f_2} = {Cc:sig4}$ cm⁻¹.

Effective focal length $f = -1/C =$ **{feff:sig3} cm**. Back focal distance $-A/C =$ **{bfd:sig3} cm** (negative means the focus is virtual, before the second lens).

drills.title: Designing an achromatic doublet
drills.prompt: Design an achromatic doublet with focal length {fmm} mm from a crown glass with Abbe number $V_1 = {V1}$ and a flint glass with $V_2 = {V2}$. Find the power of each element in diopters, to 3 significant figures (include the sign).
drills.solution:
Total power $P = 1/f = 1/({fmm}\times10^{-3}\text{ m}) = {P:sig4}$ D. Color correction needs $P_1/V_1 + P_2/V_2 = 0$ with $P_1 + P_2 = P$.

$P_1 = \dfrac{PV_1}{V_1 - V_2} =$ **{P1:sig3} D** and $P_2 = -\dfrac{PV_2}{V_1 - V_2} =$ **{P2:sig3} D**.

drills.title: Spacetime interval and proper time
drills.prompt: In Earth's frame, two events are {dx} m apart and {dt:num1} μs apart in time. Using $c = 3.00\times10^8$ m/s, find the spacetime interval $\Delta s$ between them (m, 3 significant figures) and the proper time measured by a clock that travels at constant velocity from one event to the other (μs, 3 significant figures).
drills.solution:
Light travels 300 m per μs, so $c\Delta t = 300({dt:num1}) = {cdt:sig4}$ m.

$(\Delta s)^2 = (c\Delta t)^2 - (\Delta x)^2 = {cdt:sig4}^2 - {dx}^2 > 0$, so the separation is timelike and $\Delta s =$ **{s:sig3} m**.

The clock is at rest in its own frame, so its time is $\Delta s/c = {s:sig4}/300 =$ **{tau:sig3} μs**, less than {dt:num1} μs.

drills.title: Relativistic Doppler shift
drills.prompt: A source emits {lam} (lab wavelength). It is {dir} the observer at ${b}c$, moving directly along the line of sight. Find the observed wavelength (nm, 4 significant figures) and the redshift $z = \lambda_{\text{obs}}/\lambda_{\text{src}} - 1$ (3 significant figures; negative for a blueshift).
drills.solution:
For recession $\lambda_{\text{obs}} = \lambda_{\text{src}}\sqrt{\dfrac{1 + \beta}{1 - \beta}}$; for approach the signs of $\beta$ flip.

Here $\lambda_{\text{obs}} = {L0}\sqrt{\dfrac{1 + ({sg})({b})}{1 - ({sg})({b})}} =$ **{lo:sig4} nm**.

$z = {lo:sig4}/{L0} - 1 =$ **{zz:sig3}**.

drills.title: Tunneling through a rectangular barrier
drills.prompt: An electron with energy {E:num1} eV meets a rectangular barrier {U:num1} eV high and {L:num2} nm wide. Find the decay constant $\kappa$ inside the barrier (nm⁻¹, 3 significant figures) and the transmission probability from the thick-barrier formula $T \approx 16(E/U)(1 - E/U)\,e^{-2\kappa L}$ (3 significant figures). Use $m_ec^2 = 511{,}000$ eV and $\hbar c = 197.3$ eV·nm.
drills.solution:
$U - E = {dU:num1}$ eV, so $\kappa = \dfrac{\sqrt{2(511{,}000)({dU:num1})}}{197.3} =$ **{kap:sig3} nm⁻¹**.

Prefactor: $16({E:num1}/{U:num1})(1 - {E:num1}/{U:num1}) = {pre:sig3}$. Exponent: $2\kappa L = 2({kap:sig4})({L:num2})$.

$T \approx {pre:sig3}\,e^{-2\kappa L} =$ **{T:sig3}**.

drills.title: Scanning tunneling microscope sensitivity
drills.prompt: An STM tip sits above a metal surface with work function {phi:num1} eV, which you may take as the barrier height above the tunneling electrons. The gap {up} by {dd:num2} nm. Find $\kappa$ (nm⁻¹, 3 significant figures) and the ratio of the new tunneling current to the old one (3 significant figures), taking the current proportional to $e^{-2\kappa d}$. Use $m_ec^2 = 511{,}000$ eV and $\hbar c = 197.3$ eV·nm.
drills.solution:
$\kappa = \dfrac{\sqrt{2(511{,}000)({phi:num1})}}{197.3} =$ **{kap:sig3} nm⁻¹**.

The gap {up} by $\Delta d = {dd:num2}$ nm, so the current is multiplied by $e^{-2\kappa\,\Delta d}$ with $\Delta d$ positive for a wider gap and negative for a narrower one: ratio $=$ **{ratio:sig3}**.

drills.title: Alpha decay Q-value
drills.prompt: Find the Q-value (MeV, 3 significant figures) and the alpha particle's kinetic energy (MeV, 3 significant figures) for the alpha decay of {iso}, starting at rest. Helium-4 is 4.002603 u; 1 u = 931.5 MeV/$c^2$. Share the energy using mass numbers.
drills.solution:
Mass lost: $\Delta m = {mP:dp6} - {mD:dp6} - 4.002603 = {dm:dp6}$ u.

$Q = {dm:dp6}(931.5) =$ **{Q:sig3} MeV**.

The alpha particle (mass number 4) and the daughter (mass number {A} − 4) share it in inverse proportion to their masses: $K_\alpha = Q(A - 4)/A = {Q:sig4}\cdot\dfrac{ {A} - 4}{ {A} } =$ **{Ka:sig3} MeV**.

drills.title: Liquid-drop binding energy
drills.prompt: Use the semi-empirical mass formula with $a_V = 15.75$ MeV, $a_S = 17.8$ MeV, $a_C = 0.711$ MeV, $a_A = 23.7$ MeV and $\delta = 11.18/\sqrt A$ MeV (add for even $Z$ and even $N$, subtract for odd $Z$ and odd $N$, zero for odd $A$) to estimate the binding energy of the nucleus with $Z = {Z}$ and $A = {A}$ (MeV, 4 significant figures) and its binding energy per nucleon (MeV, 3 significant figures).
drills.solution:
$Z = {Z}$, $N = {N}$.

Volume $15.75({A}) = {vol:sig4}$; surface $17.8({A})^{2/3} = {surf:sig4}$; Coulomb $0.711({Z})({Z} - 1)/{A}^{1/3} = {coul:sig4}$; asymmetry $23.7({A} - 2 \cdot {Z})^2/{A} = {asym:sig3}$; pairing ${pair:sig3}$ (all MeV).

$E_B = {vol:sig4} - {surf:sig4} - {coul:sig4} - {asym:sig3} + ({pair:sig3}) =$ **{EB:sig4} MeV**, or **{per:sig3} MeV** per nucleon.

drills.title: A charge above a grounded plane
drills.prompt: A $+{qn}$ nC point charge is held {dcm} cm above a large grounded metal plate. Using the method of images, find (a) the force on the charge in μN, (b) the induced surface charge density on the plate directly beneath the charge in μC/m² (with its sign), and (c) the work needed to move the charge very far away, in μJ. Give each to 3 significant figures ($k = 8.99\times10^9$ N·m²/C²).
drills.solution:
The image is $-{qn}$ nC at {dcm} cm below the plate, so the two charges are $2d = 2({dm})$ m apart.

(a) $F = \dfrac{kq^2}{(2d)^2} = \dfrac{(8.99\times10^9)({qn}\times10^{-9})^2}{(2 \times {dm})^2} =$ **{F:sig3} μN**, toward the plate.

(b) Directly beneath ($r = 0$): $\sigma = -\dfrac{q}{2\pi d^2} = -\dfrac{{qn}\times10^{-9}}{2\pi({dm})^2} =$ **{sig:sig3} μC/m²**.

(c) $W = \dfrac{kq^2}{4d} = \dfrac{(8.99\times10^9)({qn}\times10^{-9})^2}{4 \times {dm}} =$ **{W:sig3} μJ**, half the energy of a real pair of charges $2d$ apart.

drills.title: A charge near a grounded sphere
drills.prompt: A grounded metal sphere of radius {Rcm} cm has its center {acm} cm from a $+{qn}$ nC point charge. Find (a) the image charge in nC (with its sign), (b) its distance from the sphere's center in cm, and (c) the magnitude of the force on the point charge in μN. Give each to 3 significant figures ($k = 8.99\times10^9$ N·m²/C²).
drills.solution:
(a) $q' = -\dfrac{R}{a}\,q = -\dfrac{{Rcm}}{{acm}}({qn}\text{ nC}) =$ **{qp:sig3} nC**.

(b) $b = \dfrac{R^2}{a} = \dfrac{({Rcm})^2}{{acm}} =$ **{bcm:sig3} cm** from the center, on the line toward the charge.

(c) The charges are $a - b = {acm} - {bcm:sig4} = {sepcm:sig4}$ cm apart, so $F = \dfrac{k\,q\,|q'|}{(a - b)^2} = \dfrac{(8.99\times10^9)({qn}\times10^{-9})({qa:sig4}\times10^{-9})}{({sep:sig4})^2} =$ **{F:sig3} μN**, an attraction.

drills.title: A capacitor partly filled with a dielectric
drills.prompt: Parallel plates of area {Acm} cm² are {dmm} mm apart. A slab with dielectric constant {kap} and thickness {tmm} mm lies against one plate, with air in the rest of the gap, and the capacitor is connected to {V} V. Find (a) the capacitance in pF and (b) the voltage across the slab in volts, each to 3 significant figures ($\varepsilon_0 = 8.85\times10^{-12}$ C²/(N·m²)).
drills.solution:
(a) The air and the slab act like capacitors in series: $C = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0A}{d - t + t/\kappa}$, with $d - t + t/\kappa = {dmm} - {tmm} + {tmm}/{kap} = {eff:sig4}$ mm. So $C = \dfrac{(8.85\times10^{-12})({Acm}\times10^{-4})}{{eff:sig4}\times10^{-3}} =$ **{C:sig3} pF**.

(b) $D$ is the same in both layers, so $E$ in the slab is $1/\kappa$ of $E$ in the air, and the voltage splits in proportion to $t/\kappa$ and $d - t$: $V_{\text{slab}} = V\,\dfrac{t/\kappa}{d - t + t/\kappa} = {V}\cdot\dfrac{{tmm}/{kap}}{{eff:sig4}} =$ **{Vs:sig3} V**. The air layer takes the rest.

drills.title: Inserting a dielectric, with and without the battery
drills.prompt: A {C0} pF air capacitor is charged to {V} V. A slab with $\kappa = {kap}$ is then slid in to fill the gap. (a) If the battery was disconnected first, find the final voltage (V) and stored energy (nJ). (b) If the battery stays connected, find the final charge (nC) and stored energy (nJ). Give each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Before: $U_0 = \tfrac12C_0V^2 = \tfrac12({C0}\times10^{-12})({V})^2 = {U0:sig4}$ nJ. The slab multiplies $C$ by {kap}.

(a) Disconnected, so $Q$ is fixed: $V = {V}/{kap} =$ **{Va:sig3} V**, and $U = Q^2/(2C)$ falls by the same factor: $U = {U0:sig4}/{kap} =$ **{Ua:sig3} nJ**. The difference is work the field did pulling the slab in.

(b) Connected, so $V$ is fixed: $Q = \kappa C_0V = {kap}({C0}\text{ pF})({V}\text{ V}) =$ **{Qb:sig3} nC**, and $U = \tfrac12CV^2$ rises by the factor {kap}: **{Ub:sig3} nJ**. The battery supplied $(\kappa - 1)C_0V^2 = {Wb:sig3}$ nJ, twice the increase in stored energy.

drills.title: Energy to assemble three charges
drills.prompt: Charges of ${q1}$ μC, ${q2}$ μC and ${q3}$ μC are placed at the corners of an equilateral triangle with sides of {scm} cm. How much work does it take to assemble them, starting from very far apart? Give the answer in joules to 3 significant figures, with its sign ($k = 8.99\times10^9$ N·m²/C²).
drills.solution:
Every pair is the same distance $s = {s}$ m apart, so $U = \dfrac{k}{\,s}(q_1q_2 + q_1q_3 + q_2q_3)$.

The sum of the pair products is $({q1})({q2}) + ({q1})({q3}) + ({q2})({q3}) = {S}$ μC².

$U = \dfrac{8.99\times10^9}{{s}}({S}\times10^{-12}) =$ **{U:sig3} J**. A positive answer means work had to be done on the charges; a negative one means assembling them released energy, and that much work is needed to pull them apart again.

drills.title: Electric energy of a nucleus
drills.prompt: Model a {n} nucleus as a uniformly charged ball of radius $R = (1.2\text{ fm})A^{1/3}$. Find (a) its radius in fm and (b) its electric self-energy $\tfrac35k(Ze)^2/R$ in MeV, each to 3 significant figures. Use $ke^2 = 1.44$ MeV·fm.
drills.solution:
(a) $R = 1.2({A})^{1/3} =$ **{R:sig3} fm**.

(b) $U = \dfrac35\cdot\dfrac{(ke^2)Z^2}{\,R} = 0.6 \times \dfrac{1.44 \times {Z}^2}{{R:sig4}} =$ **{U:sig3} MeV**. (Nuclear models use $Z(Z - 1)$ instead of $Z^2$, since a proton doesn't repel itself.)

drills.title: Force between capacitor plates
drills.prompt: A parallel-plate capacitor with plates of area {Acm} cm², {dmm} mm apart, is connected to {V} V. Find (a) the electrostatic pressure on each plate in Pa and (b) the force between the plates in mN, each to 3 significant figures ($\varepsilon_0 = 8.85\times10^{-12}$ C²/(N·m²)).
drills.solution:
$E = V/d = {V}/({dmm}\times10^{-3}) = {E:sig4}$ V/m.

(a) $P = \tfrac12\varepsilon_0E^2 = \tfrac12(8.85\times10^{-12})({E:sig4})^2 =$ **{P:sig3} Pa**.

(b) $F = PA = ({P:sig4})({Acm}\times10^{-4}) =$ **{F:sig3} mN**, an attraction. (This is $\tfrac12QE$: each plate feels only the other plate's field.)

drills.title: Thévenin equivalent of two battery branches
drills.prompt: Two branches join junctions A and B: a {E1} V battery in series with {R1} Ω, and a {E2} V battery in series with {R2} Ω, both batteries with their $+$ terminal toward A. A load resistor $R_L = {RL}$ Ω is to be connected from A to B. Find the Thévenin voltage $V_A - V_B$ with the load removed (V), the Thévenin resistance (Ω), and the load current (A), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
With the load removed, node A has no net current in or out: $\dfrac{{E1} - V}{{R1}} + \dfrac{{E2} - V}{{R2}} = 0$, so $V_{\text{th}} = \dfrac{{E1}({R2}) + {E2}({R1})}{{R1} + {R2}} =$ **{Vth:sig3} V**.

Replace both batteries with wires: {R1} Ω and {R2} Ω are in parallel, $R_{\text{th}} = \dfrac{({R1})({R2})}{{R1} + {R2}} =$ **{Rth:sig3} Ω**.

$I_L = \dfrac{V_{\text{th}}}{R_{\text{th}} + R_L} = \dfrac{{Vth:sig4}}{{Rth:sig4} + {RL}} =$ **{IL:sig3} A**.

drills.title: Unbalanced Wheatstone bridge
drills.prompt: A Wheatstone bridge has an ideal {Ev} V battery across its top and bottom corners. The left side has $R_1 = {R1}$ Ω (top) and $R_2 = {R2}$ Ω (bottom) meeting at point c; the right side has $R_3 = {R3}$ Ω (top) and $R_x = {Rx}$ Ω (bottom) meeting at point d. A galvanometer of resistance {Rg} Ω joins c and d. Find $V_d - V_c$ with the galvanometer removed (V, negative if c is higher), and the size of the galvanometer current (mA), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Potentials above the bottom corner: $V_c = {Ev}\cdot\dfrac{{R2}}{{R1} + {R2}} = {Vc:sig4}$ V and $V_d = {Ev}\cdot\dfrac{{Rx}}{{R3} + {Rx}} = {Vd:sig4}$ V, so $V_d - V_c =$ **{Vth:sig3} V**.

With the battery replaced by a wire, $R_{\text{th}} = ({R1} \parallel {R2}) + ({R3} \parallel {Rx}) = {Rth:sig4}$ Ω.

$I_g = \dfrac{|V_{\text{th}}|}{R_{\text{th}} + R_g} = \dfrac{{aV:sig4}}{{Rth:sig4} + {Rg}}$ A $=$ **{Ig:sig3} mA**.

drills.title: Capacitor behind a voltage divider
drills.prompt: An ideal {Ev} V battery, a switch and $R_1 = {R1}$ kΩ are in series with a parallel pair: $R_2 = {R2}$ kΩ and an uncharged {C} μF capacitor. The switch closes at $t = 0$. Find the capacitor's final voltage (V), the time constant (ms), and the capacitor voltage at $t = {t}$ ms (V), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Final: the capacitor carries no current, so $R_1$ and $R_2$ form a divider: $V_\infty = {Ev}\cdot\dfrac{{R2}}{{R1} + {R2}} =$ **{Vinf:sig3} V**.

Seen from the capacitor (battery replaced by a wire), $R_1 \parallel R_2 = {Rth:sig4}$ kΩ, so $\tau = R_{\text{th}}C = ({Rth:sig4}\text{ k}\Omega)({C}\ \mu\text{F}) =$ **{tau:sig3} ms** (kΩ × μF = ms).

$V_C = V_\infty\left(1 - e^{-t/\tau}\right) = {Vinf:sig4}\left(1 - e^{-{t}/{tau:sig4}}\right) =$ **{VC:sig3} V**.

drills.title: Relaxation oscillator period
drills.prompt: A relaxation oscillator charges a {C} μF capacitor through {R} kΩ from an ideal {Ev} V battery. A switch across the capacitor closes when its voltage reaches {Von} V and opens when it has fallen to {Voff} V; treat the discharge as instant. Find the period (ms) and the frequency (Hz), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$RC = ({R}\text{ k}\Omega)({C}\ \mu\text{F}) = {tau:sig4}$ ms. Each charge starts at $V_{\text{off}}$ and heads for $\mathcal{E}$, reaching $V_{\text{on}}$ after

$T = RC\ln\dfrac{\mathcal{E} - V_{\text{off}}}{\mathcal{E} - V_{\text{on}}} = {tau:sig4}\ln\dfrac{{Ev} - {Voff}}{{Ev} - {Von}} =$ **{T:sig3} ms**.

$f = 1/T =$ **{f:sig3} Hz**.

drills.title: RC low-pass filter response
drills.prompt: An RC low-pass filter has $R = {R}$ kΩ and $C = {C}$ nF, with the output taken across the capacitor. Find its cutoff frequency (Hz), and for a {f} Hz sinusoidal input the gain $V_{\text{out}}/V_{\text{in}}$ and the phase lag (degrees), all to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$RC = ({R}\times10^3)({C}\times10^{-9}) = {RC:texsci}$ s, so $f_c = \dfrac{1}{2\pi RC} =$ **{fc:sig3} Hz**.

At {f} Hz: $\omega RC = 2\pi({f})({RC:texsci}) = {x:sig4}$.

Gain $= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 + ({x:sig4})^2}} =$ **{gain:sig3}**; lag $= \arctan({x:sig4}) =$ **{lag:sig3}°**.
